seniors.counts: 4-count quaternary pulse matching the zabumba downbeat.
seniors.seated_version: Sit in a circle holding hands or a light cloth tether, tapping the left foot forward on the beat.
seniors.standing_version: Stand in a stationary circle holding hands with reduced travel distance, focusing on the left-foot stamp.
seniors.tempo_and_range: Maintain slow tempo with reduced step range and smaller spatial movement.

movement_profile.arms_and_hands: holding hands in a large ring, individuals may make choreographies with hands
movement_profile.footwork: pisan forte com o pé esquerdo à frente, dois passos para trás e dois passos para a frente
movement_profile.formation_and_space: large ring on beaches and squares, moving to the right, inner ring forms if too large
movement_profile.partnering: community circle with no fixed partners

signature_moves.description: Stepping clockwise in the circle while stamping the left foot forward on the heavy zabumba beat, moving two steps back and two steps forward.
signature_moves.name: Left-foot stamp and step sequence

music_profile.rhythm_pattern: toque grave da zabumba na cabeça do compasso e toques abafados nos outros tempos
music_profile.sound_description: A slow, unhurried quaternary pulse driven by the heavy bass thud of the zabumba on beat one, surrounded by the dry rattle of the ganzá and maracá, while a lead singer carries a repetitive, call-and-response refrain.
music_profile.vocal_style: entoada pelo mestre cirandeiro with simple melodies and refrains

basic_steps: Hold hands in a circle facing the center
Stamp firmly with the left foot forward on the zabumba downbeat
teaching.formation: large open circle holding hands, with nested inner rings if the crowd expands
teaching.level_notes: Accessible to all ages and experience levels with no technical prerequisites
